title: Run a Real AI Model on Your Own Laptop — Free and Offline
description: You don't need a subscription or a data center to use a capable AI model. This video explains what you need to run one on your own laptop, for free.

shots.text: You don't need a data center to run a capable AI model. You need the laptop you already own.

props.headline: RUN AI OFFLINE
props.subline: on the laptop you already own

shots.text: Open models now run fully offline, with no subscription.
And your notes and code never leave your machine.

props.text: Your data stays on your disk

shots.text: You need three things. A tool, a model, and enough memory.
Start with the tool. Ollama is free, and one command downloads a model and starts a chat.
Prefer a chat window? LM Studio is also free, and works like the apps you already use.

messages.text: Here are the three decisions you made...

shots.text: Next, the model. Size is measured in billions of parameters.
Bigger models are smarter, but they need much more memory.
The trick is quantization. It stores each weight in fewer bits, so the file gets much smaller.
The cost is a small drop in quality, which most people never notice in everyday use.
Open models have also become far more efficient in the last few years.
Finally, memory. An 8B model at 4-bit fits comfortably in 16 gigabytes of RAM.
Here is a quick checklist before you start.

items.text: About 10 GB of free disk space

shots.text: A graphics card is optional. Without one, answers simply arrive more slowly.
As one project puts it, the best model is the one you can actually run.

props.text: The best model is the one you can actually run.

shots.text: My advice? Start with a small model, check that it is fast enough, then try a bigger one.
Which model would you try first? Tell me in the comments, and subscribe for more practical AI.
